content: Cystex, a combination of methenamine, sodium salicylate, and benzoic acid, is prescribed for specific indications and requires careful administration. The recommended dosage for individuals aged 16 years and older is two tablets taken orally every six hours, with meals and at bedtime. It should only be used after a urinary tract infection (UTI) has been eradicated with appropriate antibiotics. The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established for individuals under 16 years of age. Methenamine is indicated for the prophylaxis and suppression of chronic, recurrent UTIs when long-term therapy is necessary. Sodium salicylate serves as an analgesic, while benzoic acid exhibits weak antifungal and antibacterial properties and aids in acidifying the urine. During pregnancy, Cystex is classified as Category C, meaning caution is advised as the risk to the fetus cannot be ruled out. Methenamine is excreted in human breast milk, so caution is also recommended during lactation due to potential risks to the infant. Pharmacokinetically, methenamine is well absorbed, with 10-30% hydrolyzed by gastric acid unless the tablet is enteric-coated. Its half-life is approximately 3-6 hours. Peak urinary concentrations of formaldehyde occur within two hours for hippurate salts and 3-8 hours for mandelate salts. The drug undergoes partial metabolism in the liver (10-25%) and is primarily excreted in the urine (90%). In acidic urine, methenamine is hydrolyzed into ammonia and formaldehyde, which act as bactericidal agents. However, it does not convert to formaldehyde in the serum.
